public_rationale: This is mainly a forecast with no deadline: the agents executives describe 'cannot exist, and will never exist.' His next sentence admits Operator exists but 'does not work'. So the test is whether agents exist that reliably do the complex delegated web work executives describe, not whether any web agent exists. Independent, human-checked testing shows top agents doing well on easy live-web tasks but struggling on harder ones (e1). I found no independent evidence, by the evaluation date, of agents reliably doing such work in broad use. That leaves his forecast unrefuted, but a date can never confirm 'never'. So it stays open.
limitations: Where 'fantastical' begins is the evaluator's reading. He did not define it.
The newest independent human-checked results I could cite are from 2025. 2026 leaderboard figures were unverified.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The fantastical 'agents on the internet' do not exist, cannot exist, and will never exist.

statement.excerpt: It’s also weird that we’re still having a debate about “the power of AI” and “what agents might do in the future” based on fantastical thoughts about “agents on the internet” that do not exist, cannot exist, and will never exist, and it’s fucking weird that executives and members of the media keep acting as if that’s the case.

from_speaker: fantastical thoughts about "agents on the internet"
do not exist, cannot exist, and will never exist
executives and members of the media keep acting as if that's the case
next sentence: OpenAI's Operator Agent does not work; AI browsers are fundamentally broken
our_interpretation: He admits that basic web agents like Operator exist ('does not work'). So 'do not exist' cannot mean any web agent at all. It means the 'fantastical' agents executives describe.

Reading in his terms: autonomous agents that reliably carry out the complex, delegated, multi-step work on the open web that executives and the media promise, not demos or tools that only partly work.
'Will never exist' has no deadline. It cannot be confirmed by any date. It can only be shown false by such agents actually existing.
criteria.support_condition: The claim can never be fully confirmed by a date. Ongoing evidence that the best web agents still fail often on realistic live-web tasks is consistent with it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Agents are widely available and independently shown to reliably do the complex, delegated multi-step web work executives describe, at about the reliability of a human assistant.
